title: Apple Oat Crumble
summary: Chunks of mixed apples baked under a clumpy oat, brown sugar and nut topping until the fruit is tender and bubbling.

ingredients.item: mixed sweet and tart apples such as Golden Delicious and Granny Smith (about 7)
fine sea salt or table salt

steps.title: Prepare the apples
steps.text: Heat the oven to 190 °C (170 °C fan) and butter the dish. Peel and core the apples, cut into 2-3 cm chunks and toss with the brown sugar, cinnamon, cornflour and lemon juice, then spread in the dish. Mixing sweet and tart varieties gives both soft and firmer pieces.

steps.title: Make the crumble
steps.text: Mix the flour, oats, brown sugar, nuts if using and salt, then stir in the melted butter with a fork until evenly moist. Squeeze into clumps of different sizes and scatter over the apples. Clumps give a crisp, craggy top instead of a sandy one.

steps.title: Bake
steps.text: Set the dish on the tray and bake 45-55 min until the topping is deep golden, the juices bubble at the edge and a knife slides easily into the apples. The tray catches any drips, and bubbling juices mean the cornflour has thickened.

steps.title: Rest and serve
steps.text: Cool 15 min so the juices settle, then serve warm with plain yoghurt or whipped cream. Serves 6. Keep covered in the fridge up to 3 days and reheat at 180 °C (160 °C fan) 15 min.

tips: Common mistake: cutting the apples too small. Chunks of 2-3 cm keep some shape and bite.
Leave the nuts out for a nut-free crumble; add 50 g more oats instead.
Squeeze the topping into clumps for the crunchiest result.
Don't taste the raw dough or batter: raw flour and raw egg aren't safe to eat until baked.
storage: Keep covered in the fridge up to 3 days and reheat at 180 °C (160 °C fan) about 15 min until hot. Freeze baked up to 2 months.
